title: Remote Entanglement of Solid-State Spin Qubits Integrated in Broadband Waveguides
authors: Christopher Waas, Timo Dolné, Hans K. C. Beukers, Alexander M. Stramma, Nina Codreanu, Noé Mathieu, Ronald Hanson
abstract: Solid-state spin-photon interfaces promise to scale quantum networks through on-chip photonic integration and multiplexed entanglement generation. To date, remote entanglement between integrated emitters has been realized only in cavity-enhanced systems, where fabrication yield and spectral matching remain major obstacles. Here we demonstrate heralded remote entanglement between diamond tin-vacancy spin qubits embedded in separate on-chip waveguides. Combining intrinsically efficient photon emission with a broadband waveguide architecture provides high device yield and obviates the need for spectral matching to cavity modes. We realize coherent optical and spin control and achieve high-visibility two-photon interference. By combining photon-mediated entanglement generation with real-time feedforward, we produce a consistent entangled state independent of the heralding pattern. These results establish waveguide-integrated tin-vacancy centers as a compelling platform for scalable quantum network nodes.
summary: The research demonstrates scalable methods for generating remote entanglement between solid-state spin qubits ($	ext{SnV}$ centers) integrated into on-chip broadband waveguides. By circumventing the need for spectral matching to optical cavities, they achieve high-fidelity two-photon interference and heralded entanglement generation. This establishes a robust platform for building quantum network nodes.
main_problem: The primary goal is to demonstrate scalable quantum network links by achieving remote entanglement between solid-state spin qubits integrated into broadband waveguides, overcoming limitations of previous cavity-enhanced systems.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated heralded remote spin-spin entanglement using the waveguide platform, achieving high two-photon interference visibility comparable to cavity records without needing spectral matching.
method: Entanglement is generated via a photon-mediated process (Barrett-Kok protocol) involving single-photon emission from diamond tin-vacancy ($	ext{SnV}$) centers and subsequent quantum interference measurements.
model_or_system: The platform utilizes $	ext{SnV}$ spin qubits embedded in separate on-chip broadband waveguides fabricated on a high-purity diamond chip, operating at cryogenic temperatures. This system allows for intrinsic photon emission coupled to the waveguide mode.
key_observables: Entanglement fidelity ($F$), two-photon interference visibility ($V$), single-photon detection probability density, and spin coherence time ($T_{2	ext{DD}}$).
important_parameters: Operating temperature of $1	ext{ K}$; high structural yield (99%); entanglement success probability limited by photon collection efficiency ($\approx 0.3\%$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that broadband waveguides provide sufficient coupling and low loss to enable scalable, high-yield integration compared to cavity methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the platform schematic (Fig. 1), qubit characterization (Rabi oscillations, coherence time scaling in Fig. 2), two-photon interference measurements showing visibility vs. time difference (Fig. 3), and the full heralded entanglement sequence (Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the fundamental properties of the $	ext{SnV}$ qubits (coherence, photon emission) in waveguides, demonstrating high-visibility two-photon interference without cavities, and culminating in the realization and characterization of heralded remote spin-spin entanglement.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical implementation challenges for quantum networking nodes by replacing fragile cavity coupling with robust waveguide integration, a critical step for scaling solid-state quantum technologies.
